existing_nonduplicate_basis.nonduplication_note: The matched-baseline preregistration already separates a common canonical primary arm from candidate-native template sensitivity. This delta does not create another baseline protocol. It closes the remaining transport gap from that evaluation-only renderer to the actual future Xeno/ClayCode model-facing renderer required by the finished runtime.

observed_gap.finding: A checkpoint can rank well under COMMON_CANONICAL_EVAL_RENDER/v1 yet regress or reorder under the final Xeno/ClayCode renderer. Therefore a matched-baseline winner is at most provisional until renderer transportability is checked at exact renderer/tokenizer/input identity.
why_material: The current architecture requires Xeno/ClayCode to be the sole addressable model-facing cognitive semantics.
The current common canonical evaluation renderer is explicitly not the final Xeno ABI.
Qwen3.5-0.8B and Qwen3.5-0.8B-Base carry materially different native chat-template behavior, demonstrating that formatting/control-token semantics are not a neutral implementation detail.
Dynamic-binding training is specifically vulnerable to stable renderer-position, field-name and control-token shortcuts.

external_method_evidence.source: Hugging Face Transformers chat templating documentation
external_method_evidence.finding: Chat models are trained on model-specific token/control-token formats; using the wrong template can materially degrade performance.
external_method_evidence.project_implication: Renderer identity must be treated as an execution/evaluation factor, not hidden behind semantic prompt equivalence.

external_method_evidence.finding: The post-trained 0.8B tokenizer carries a role-aware chat template with explicit system/user/assistant control structure and generation-prompt behavior.
external_method_evidence.project_implication: Native-template performance is a bundle property of model plus tokenizer plus renderer.

external_method_evidence.finding: The base 0.8B tokenizer template is much simpler and primarily renders the supplied message content rather than the post-trained role/control structure.
external_method_evidence.project_implication: Native-template arms are not a weight-only comparison and cannot silently determine the checkpoint winner.

external_method_evidence.source: Voronov, Wolf, Ryabinin (2024), Mind Your Format: Towards Consistent Evaluation of In-Context Learning Improvements
external_method_evidence.finding: Prompt/template format can materially alter measured performance and can change which setup appears strongest.
external_method_evidence.project_implication: Checkpoint ranking must be tested for renderer transport rather than assumed invariant.

external_method_evidence.source: Wu, Geiger, Milliere (2025), How Do Transformers Learn Variable Binding in Symbolic Programs?
external_method_evidence.finding: Transformers can pass through shallow heuristic phases before systematic variable-binding mechanisms emerge.
external_method_evidence.project_implication: A renderer that exposes stable nuisance structure can reward shallow binding shortcuts even when semantic binding is the intended capability.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Checkpoint ordering and hard-axis eligibility under COMMON_CANONICAL_EVAL_RENDER/v1 will mostly transport to the frozen Xeno/ClayCode renderer once semantic task content is preserved and exact consumed-input identity is bound.
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: At least one candidate will change rank or hard-axis eligibility because renderer/control-token structure interacts strongly with its pre/post-training history.
hypotheses.discriminator: After the Xeno/ClayCode renderer ABI is frozen, rerun a paired preregistered subset of the same family-disjoint logical cases for all ABI-eligible candidates under both COMMON_CANONICAL_EVAL_RENDER/v1 and the exact Xeno/ClayCode renderer. Bind renderer digest, rendered UTF-8 digest, tokenizer digest, input tensor identity, decoding parameters and evaluator digest per call.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Dynamic episode-local binding competence will remain above nuisance challengers under the final Xeno/ClayCode renderer.
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: Stable ClayCode field positions, control tokens, delimiters or atom presentation create a new shortcut that restores apparent accuracy without semantic-case dependence.
hypotheses.discriminator: For the frozen renderer, require semantic ablation with renderer structure preserved, S3 mapping equivariance, field/order perturbations where semantically legal, atom/symbol counterbalance, tokenizer-level target leakage scans and shallow renderer-only nuisance challengers. Semantic ablation or renderer-only predictors must remain near chance while full semantic cases retain the required capability.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Training examples materialized through the exact future Xeno/ClayCode renderer will reduce interface mismatch compared with training on evaluation-only canonical scaffolds.
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: Renderer-specific training will overfit interface syntax and harm transfer/retention, while semantic normalization is sufficient.
hypotheses.discriminator: Only after positive data admission and training authority open, compare matched adaptation schedules that differ only in renderer exposure. Evaluate frozen semantic binding transfer, exact Xeno packet compliance, abstention/epistemics, general reasoning retention and renderer perturbation robustness.

required_inputs: frozen Xeno/ClayCode renderer version and digest
family-disjoint paired logical-case subset not used for prompt tuning
frozen deterministic evaluators and catastrophic-error taxonomy

paired_arms.purpose: retain comparability with the existing preregistered checkpoint baseline
measure transport into the actual intended model-facing runtime language
diagnostic capability-ceiling/sensitivity arm already anticipated by the baseline preregistration

report_per_candidate: hard-axis minimum under A and B
overall worst-axis under A and B
catastrophic error count under A and B
exact rendered-byte and token-tensor identity receipts
fail_closed_rules: Do not call a checkpoint final if it is eligible under A but fails a required hard axis under B.
Any new catastrophic epistemic/authority error under B blocks final renderer compatibility for that candidate.
If candidate ranking materially changes between A and B, preserve NO_FINAL_WINNER and report renderer dependence instead of averaging the arms.
Do not repair a losing candidate with candidate-specific prompt edits after the paired renderer subset is opened.
Do not promote renderer-only or semantic-ablation performance as evidence of true dynamic binding.
Do not admit training rows merely because renderer transport testing exists.

architecture_to_training_reinjection.runtime_change: Final Xeno/ClayCode renderer ABI is part of the executable Xeno shell/interface, not cosmetic prompt text.
architecture_to_training_reinjection.required_trigger2_delta: Whenever the renderer ABI materially changes, invalidate or version the renderer-transport receipt and rerun the paired transport subset before claiming final checkpoint/training-substrate compatibility.
architecture_to_training_reinjection.dataset_rule: Future admitted SFT examples must record the exact renderer version/digest used for model-visible materialization. Evaluation-only canonical scaffolds must not silently become production-training format.
architecture_to_training_reinjection.jspace_rule: Any post-FT J-Space/vector result is additionally bound to the exact renderer/input identity because control effects may be input-distribution dependent.

execution_decision.reason: Current authority keeps provider routes hard-off and does not admit training/model execution in this cycle. This delta is source/research only.
